headline: Every major reclaims its 200-day at once, but RSI readings above 80 mean this move is stretched
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it flipped hard. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB are all above their 200-day lines, with DOGE and ADA the lone holdouts still underneath theirs. That is seven majors mostly aligned to the upside, a very different picture from a market where trend lines disagree. BTC is up 6.49% on the day and 23.05% over 30 days, ETH is up 5.64% on the day and a striking 40.88% over the month, and even the laggards DOGE and ADA are posting double-digit daily gains despite sitting well below their long-term averages. When nearly everything moves the same direction this fast, the question stops being about direction and starts being about how much fuel is left in the tank.

That is where momentum gets interesting, because it is flashing a warning most trend-followers know well. RSI-14 on BTC sits at 85.7, ETH at 87.3, SOL at 82.3, XRP at 83.2, BNB at 81.2, DOGE at 81.5. Anything north of 70 is conventionally considered overbought; these are readings you see when a rally is running hot, not resting. MACD is above signal on every single asset, confirming the trend is still technically intact and accelerating by that measure. So you have trend and momentum agreeing on direction but momentum screaming that the move has outrun itself. That is not a contradiction to explain away, it is the defining tension of today's tape: strength and stretch, both real, at the same time.

Positioning adds texture rather than resolving it. Funding across BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and DOGE all sits at a modest 0.01% per 8 hours (11% annualized), which is unremarkable, not the kind of expensive, crowded-long funding that usually precedes a shakeout. But the long/short account ratios tell a more skewed story: DOGE traders are leaning long at 3.45 to 1, SOL at 1.81 to 1, XRP at 1.45 to 1. Liquidations lean short-heavy almost everywhere (ETH shorts took $11.1M in losses against $2.6M for longs over 8 hours; SOL shorts lost $9.6M against $2.1M for longs), meaning the people caught wrong-footed by this rally have mostly been short sellers getting squeezed, not longs getting flushed. Cheap funding plus a short squeeze in progress is a specific kind of fuel, not obviously fragile yet, but not resting either.

Flows are where the greed reading gets contradicted. Whale wallets moved a net $392.6 million onto exchanges in the last 24 hours, split between $230.9 million of BTC and $161.6 million of ETH, and the weekly pattern backs this up: after two weeks of coins moving off exchanges (week ending Jul 31: $1,058M off; week ending Aug 07: $316M off), the last two weeks reversed to onto-exchange flows ($405M week ending Aug 14, $553M week ending Aug 21). Moving coin onto exchanges is typically a precursor to selling, or at minimum active repositioning, and it is happening while prices rip higher. Meanwhile the traditional-finance bid is unambiguous: BTC ETFs took in $606.3 million on 20 Aug 2026, part of $1,554.1 million over the last five sessions with 4 of those days net positive; ETH ETFs added $219.5 million on the same day, $508.6 million over five sessions, also 4 days positive. So spot ETF buyers are net accumulating while whale wallets are net moving supply toward exchanges. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is essentially flat over 30 days at -0.11%, sitting at $307.7 billion, which does not suggest a fresh wave of sideline cash rushing in to chase this.

Sentiment, for once, is not out ahead of the tape: Fear & Greed sits at 72 (Greed), right at the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 72. The crowd feels exactly as good as the price action looks. That alignment between sentiment and price is worth noting precisely because the underlying signals disagree with each other: overbought RSI against confirmed MACD, ETF inflows against exchange-bound whale flows, short squeeze liquidations against merely average funding. What to watch from here: whether RSI cools without prices breaking down (a rest, not a reversal), whether the exchange-inflow trend from the last two weekly prints extends into a third week, and whether funding rates move off their current calm 0.01% reading as the crowd's optimism either gets validated or tested.
